about.metaDescription: Three brothers from Sweden, an idea on a boat and seven versions of a recipe. How MOAR came to be.

opening.body: We just wanted to get through the afternoon without a coffee in one hand and a snack in the other. Then we couldn't stop thinking about it.

chapters.label: Every afternoon
chapters.body: As students our afternoons looked the same: a coffee, then something to eat, then another coffee. Two things, two queues, every single day.

chapters.label: One summer
chapters.body: The idea came on a boat ride one summer. We got talking about our afternoons, the coffee and the snack, and someone asked: why can't they be one thing? We haven't stopped talking about it since.

chapters.label: Seven versions
chapters.body: Getting it right took two suppliers and about seven versions of the recipe. Too chalky, too sweet, too dry. We kept going until it tasted like something you'd want anyway.

chapters.label: One flavour
chapters.body: We could have launched ten. We'd rather get one exactly right.

items.title: It has to taste like a treat.
items.body: If we wouldn't eat it on a day off, it wasn't ready.

items.title: One bar, not two things.
items.body: The kick and the snack in one wrapper, or no bar at all.

items.title: Nothing we can't explain.
items.body: Every ingredient is there for a reason, and we'll tell you what it is.

science.metaDescription: Why guarana, why caffeine with protein, why 3 PM, and the numbers behind every choice in a MOAR bar.

open.body: Every MOAR bar starts with guarana, a red berry from the Amazon that looks back at you. Its seeds hold about twice the caffeine of a coffee bean.
open.berryAlt: A guarana fruit splitting open to show a black seed in white flesh, like an eye

items.title: Stronger than coffee
items.body: Guarana seeds hold about 2–4% caffeine, around twice a coffee bean. So less than half a gram of extract (0.75% of the bar) is enough for 90 mg.

items.title: You eat it, not drink it
items.body: Caffeine taken with food usually reaches its peak more slowly than on an empty stomach. In MOAR it comes wrapped in protein, fat and fibre.

items.title: The gentle reputation
items.body: In the seed, guarana's caffeine sits alongside tannins, which is often given as the reason it feels smoother. Research on that is still mixed, so we'll just say: try it.

combo.titleA: Two things you already reach for.
combo.body: Caffeine gives you the lift. Protein makes it a real snack instead of just a drink. Together, one bar does the job of both.
combo.tableTitle: The kick of one. The snack of the other.
combo.note: A filter coffee (about 200 ml) and a typical 55 g protein bar; values are typical and vary by brand. Protein contributes to the maintenance of muscle mass.

fit.body: Your body clears about half of the caffeine every five hours or so. Have the bar mid-afternoon and most of it is gone by bedtime.
fit.bigB: two thirds of it is gone.
fit.note: Based on one 90 mg bar and a typical half-life of about 5 hours; it varies between people. If you're sensitive to caffeine, have it earlier in the day.

items.q: Is guarana caffeine different from coffee caffeine?
items.a: No. It's the same molecule, C₈H₁₀N₄O₂. What's different is what comes with it: in MOAR, protein, fat and fibre instead of a cup of hot water.

While you're awake, a molecule called adenosine builds up in your brain and tells it you're getting tired. Caffeine has a similar shape, so it sits in the same spots and blocks that signal for a while. It doesn't add energy; it holds off the feeling of tiredness.
Caffeine usually peaks within about an hour, and your body clears half of it roughly every five hours. That varies a lot from person to person.

items.q: Can I have it with my coffee?
items.a: Yes. Just count the bar as another cup: 90 mg. Two coffees and a bar is 270 mg, well under the 400 mg a day the EU considers fine for healthy adults.

items.q: Will I get used to it?
items.a: A bit. People who have caffeine every day build up some tolerance, so the same amount feels milder. A few days with less caffeine resets it.

No. It's a polyol (a "sugar alcohol") made from starch. It counts as carbohydrate but not as sugar, and has about 2.4 kcal per gram instead of 4. Like other polyols, a lot at once can have a laxative effect.
Plenty of people take caffeine before they train. If you do, eat the bar 30–60 minutes before, since that's when caffeine usually peaks.
Collagen peptides give the bar its soft, chewy bite. Together with whey, milk and soy protein they make up the 14 g.
Not vegan: it contains milk and collagen. It is gluten free and made without GMOs. It contains milk and soy, and may contain peanuts and nuts.
It isn't recommended for children or pregnant women, because of the caffeine.
